To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relaxation polarization parameters can be determined from the frequency–temperature behavior of the imaginary part of the impedance in dielectrics in the high-frequency range, provided that the imaginary part has three extrema.

in dielectrics that are characterized by high electrical conduction, the parameters of relaxation processes can be determined from the frequency dependences only if there is strong polarization, and in the case of weak relaxation processes, it is necessary to determine the parameters from the frequency behavior first of the imaginary part of the electrical impedance module and then from the frequency dependence of dielectric loss tangent, taking into account that in the presence of high conduction, the frequency dependence of this parameter can contain three maxima.

the relaxation polarization parameters of dielectrics with a high conductivity can be obtained by analyzing the frequency dependence of electrical impedance and the temperature dependences of the electrical conductivity and dielectric loss tangent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method of determining the relaxation time and energy of activation of relaxation processes from the frequency behavior in a dielectric with high electrical conductivity.
a study of the frequency behavior of dielectric loss tangent in a wide temperature range for dielectrics with a high electrical conductivity.
a new method for determining the relaxation polarization parameters of dielectrics with a high steady leakage of current.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parameters of the polarization processes in dielectrics are determined by the behavior of the imaginary part of the electrical modulus or the impedance in the frequency domain.
the frequency–temperature dependence of the dieletric loss tangent is the most reliable way to determine the relaxation parameters in dielectries with high electrical conductivity.
the parameters of relaxation polarization processes in dielectrics are best determined from the frequency dependences in the dielectric loss modulus or impedance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parameters of relaxation processes can be determined from the behavior of the imaginary part of the complex impedance or the complex modulus in dielectrics having high electrical conductivity.
the relaxation polarization parameters are best determined using the frequency dependences for the imaginary parts of both the electrical module and impedance.
the frequency dependence of these parameters can be used as a tool for the identification of the relaxation polarization processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relaxation parameters in dielectries with high electrical conductivity can be determined by analyzing the frequency dependences not of the dielectric losses, but of the imaginary parts (or the real parts) of the electrical module (or the impedance).
the relaxation time of the polarization processes is determined using the frequency dependence of electrical conductivity.
the frequency dependences can be used to determine the parameters of the dielectric polarization processes in dielectrics that exhibit high electrical conductivity.
